summary: The Silver Temple (Wat Sri Suphan) presents the Lanna Craft Wisdom Museum in Wua Lai as a living craft space, with artisans demonstrating repoussé metalwork and a hands-on workshop making an engraved metal piece. This is the best-supported route to experience Chiang Mai silverwork; confirm the workshop is running before making a special trip.
whyGo: See a working craft tradition in its historic Wua Lai community, rather than only browsing finished silver.
The temple describes both live demonstrations and guided hands-on repoussé work, connecting craft with Lanna community and religious heritage.
bestFor: Visitors interested in traditional techniques, local craft, and a small take-home piece.
A flexible add-on to Wua Lai and the Silver Temple; suitable for a short cultural outing if the workshop is operating.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed, bookable class with a published price or fixed duration.
You cannot confirm the workshop in advance and have limited time for a potentially temple-only visit.
duration: Allow 1–2 hours as a planning estimate for the museum, demonstration, and possible short workshop; the operator does not publish a class duration.
cost: The temple lists museum admission as free. Workshop fee and any material charge are not published; confirm directly before participating.
hours: The temple lists daily opening hours of 06:00–18:00. These are temple hours, not confirmed workshop hours; ask when artisans and classes are available.
bestTime: Visit in daylight and contact the temple first to coordinate with the workshop. Saturday can pair naturally with the Wua Lai Walking Street, but workshop availability then is unconfirmed.
gettingThere: At Wat Sri Suphan, 100 Wua Lai Road, about 1 km south of Chiang Mai Gate. The temple suggests a red songthaew, tuk-tuk, or Grab; ask for Silver Temple / Wat Sri Suphan.
booking: No public booking procedure or class schedule was found. Contact the temple at 061 403 2815 or through its official visit page to ask about workshop dates, language, group size, fee, and materials. Do not assume a walk-in lesson is available.
accessibility: The temple asks visitors to cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes before entering buildings. The Silver Ubosot is traditionally closed to women; this restriction concerns the ubosot, while the museum/workshop access arrangements are not specified. Ask about step-free access and seating before visiting.
practicalTips: Ask whether the session is an actual participant workshop or an artisan demonstration, and what finished item and materials are included.
Wear modest clothing and comfortable shoes that are easy to remove.
Combine with nearby Wua Lai sights; the temple is identified as a Saturday Walking Street highlight.
decemberNotes: No December 2026 workshop schedule or holiday closure notice was found. Confirm dates and hours close to travel; the temple’s current daily hours do not guarantee daily craft sessions.
uncertainties: The official site describes a hands-on workshop, short courses, and live demonstrations, but gives no current fee, duration, capacity, language, booking method, or confirmed operating dates.
The official visitor page provides temple access details but does not explain accessibility within the museum/workshop.

The photo reference is a third-party image of a participant doing silverwork at Wat Sri Suphan; it is illustrative and does not establish that the same session or arrangement is currently offered. Reuse permission is not established.
